# BETWEEN SHELVES — client facts and archive boundaries

## Project
- Project name: BETWEEN SHELVES.
- Programme phrase: Four places, five units.
- Project type: community-reading furniture integrated with retained bookcases.
- Archival place: Thomas Hughes Public Library, Central Avenue, Rugby, Morgan County, Tennessee.
- Furniture scope: complete new reading seats and small furniture accessories.
- Decision: furniture arrangement and development for short browsing, companion reading and waiting.

## Archive records
| Attachment | Record | Content | Date and authorship | Image preparation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 03-archive-plan.png | HABS TENN-200, sheet 2 | Complete measured floor-plan sheet | Judson Mc Intire, East Tennessee Project, 1973 | Full original image uniformly reduced; original scale bar retained on its sheet |
| 04-archive-section.png | HABS TENN-200, sheet 4 | Complete measured longitudinal-section sheet | Judson Mc Intire, East Tennessee Project, 1973 | Full original image uniformly reduced; original scale bar retained on its sheet |
| 05-archive-interior.png | HABS TN-200-8 | General interior view from northeast | Photograph date unconfirmed in supplied metadata | Encoding from the downloaded 1920-pixel Commons preview |
- Geometry reference: measured drawings, with their original proportions and scale bars.
- Visible bookcase identity and relationships: interior photograph.
- Temporal basis: archival drawing records and an independently dated photograph record.
- Book spines in proposed scenes: neutral sample spines within retained shelf geometry.

## Room dimensions
| Record | Value | Planning meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Floor-plan long overall dimension | 30 feet 3.5 inches | Outer drawing dimension |
| Floor-plan short overall dimension | 22 feet 4 inches | Outer drawing dimension; nominal planning reference |
| Short-side dimension-chain total | 22 feet 3 inches | Source dimension-chain total |
| Short-side difference | 1 inch | Difference between the stated overall dimension and chain total |
| Main floor-to-ceiling interval | 13 feet 0 inches | Section dimension |
| Foot conversion | 1 foot = 304.8 mm | Unit conversion |
| Inch conversion | 1 inch = 25.4 mm | Unit conversion |
- Furniture planning boundary: unchanged drawn inner room boundary.
- Pixel-measured dimensions: approximate archive-derived values.

## Retained room and collection geometry
- Retained elements: drawn room boundary, entrance and other openings, door swings, windows, built-in partitions and cupboards.
- Bookcase retention: every existing footprint, bay and shelf tier; both faces of projecting cases; wall cases; usable book-storage length and depth.
- Collection capacity basis: retained shelf geometry.
- Historic context: existing wall and ceiling finishes, case cornices and incidental pictures.
- Existing movable tables, chairs, loose stools and pictured ladder: contextual furniture, optional in the proposed occupied arrangement.
- New furniture relationship: floor-supported units separated from retained bookcases; connections within new furniture and optionally between new units.
- Existing bookcases and historic finishes: retained fabric.

## Furniture programme
| ID | Unit | Quantity | Sitting places | Fixed target |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| S1 | Single-person reading seat | 1 | 1 | Clear seat 480 mm wide by 440 mm deep; height 450 mm above local floor |
| S2 | Single-person reading seat | 1 | 1 | Clear seat 480 mm wide by 440 mm deep; height 450 mm above local floor |
| C1 | Two-person companion seat | 1 | 2 | Each place clear 480 mm wide by 440 mm deep; height 450 mm above local floor |
| A1 | Shared book-support accessory | 1 | 0 | Open sample book 320 mm wide by 240 mm deep; support surface height 650 mm |
| A2 | Shared bag-rest accessory | 1 | 0 | Two upright sample bags simultaneously, each 300 mm wide by 180 mm deep by 400 mm high |
- Total: five physical furniture units and four sitting places.
- Seat dimensions: nominal client targets.
- Open design variables: seat backs and arms, profiles, footprints, legs, finishes and placement.
- Accessory relationship: at least one accessory beside an identifiable retained bookcase end and related to the new seating, with a dimensioned separation and accessible shelf faces.
- Design relationship: one coordinated furniture set.

## Passage and retrieval
- Public passage target: continuous nominal 1200 mm from the retained entrance approach into the central reading area, ending before the rear book-retrieval band.
- Entrance opening: existing drawn width.
- Retrieval target: nominal 900 mm approach band at every accessible bookcase face, including both sides of projecting cases.
- Furniture, stored bags and occupied seating envelopes: outside passage bands, retrieval bands and door swings.
- Passage and retrieval bands: adjoining or shared circulation space where their routes meet.
- Retrieval scene: lower or middle shelf access with a separate passing route.

## Connections and materials
- Support: independent floor support for every new unit.
- New joints: removable mechanical connections within new furniture and, where selected, between new units.
- Floor contact: protective feet.
- Upholstered contact: at least one sitting-contact element removable for replacement.
- Material allocation: structure; sitting contact; book and bag contact; feet and joints.
- Timber material fields: species or board type; surface finish.
- Metal material fields: metal type; surface finish.
- Upholstery material fields: fibre composition; weight in g/m2; removable element or cover construction.
- Connection fields: hardware type and count; servicing tool; access; largest disassembled component dimensions.
- Staff tasks: wiping accessible new surfaces and handling a designed removable cover.
- Technician tasks: structural joint servicing.
- Maintenance scope: routine cleaning of proposed surfaces and replacement access for new components.

## Staged use records
| State | Occupants and activity | Seats | Book and bags |
|---|---|---|---|
| Retrieval | One person retrieves a book from a lower or middle shelf; a second person passes independently | Same furniture positions as the room arrangement | One neutral sample book in retrieval |
| Solo | One person reads at S1 | S2 empty; C1 unoccupied | One sample bag in A2 |
| Companion | Two people read together at C1 | S1 empty; S2 empty | Open sample book on A1; two sample bags in A2 |
- Scene count: three separate staged illustrations.
- Figure treatment: realistic or diagrammatic figures.

## Source credit and provenance
- Credit: Historic American Buildings Survey, National Park Service, Library of Congress.
- Drawing credit: Thomas Hughes Public Library, HABS TENN-200, sheets 2 and 4, Judson Mc Intire, East Tennessee Project 1973.
- Photograph credit: interior photograph HABS TN-200-8, date unconfirmed in supplied metadata.
- Original government documentation: public domain.
- Archive image derivation: faithful reductions and encoding of the original records.
- Primary collection rights: https://www.nps.gov/subjects/heritagedocumentation/collection.htm
- Original catalogue identity: https://www.loc.gov/item/tn0110/
- Commons source and exact source-file records: supplied manifest.

steps.userMessage:
BETWEEN SHELVES | Reading seats and accessories for a retained library interior

Develop a coordinated furniture set around the retained bookcases of Thomas Hughes Public Library, Central Avenue, Rugby, Morgan County, Tennessee, using the attached archival geometry. The programme comprises two separate single-person reading seats S1 and S2, one two-person companion seat C1, one shared book support A1 and one shared bag rest A2: five physical units and four sitting places. Each place has a nominal clear sitting area 480 mm wide by 440 mm deep, at 450 mm above its local floor. A1 supports an open book 320 mm wide by 240 mm deep on a surface at 650 mm. A2 accommodates two upright bags simultaneously, each 300 mm wide by 180 mm deep by 400 mm high. Print "BETWEEN SHELVES" and "Four places, five units" on the furniture overview and presentation cover.

The bookcases anchor this project. Retain the drawn inner room boundary, openings, door swings, windows, built-in partitions and cupboards, every case footprint and every shelf tier, including both faces of projecting cases and the storage length and depth of wall cases. Reserve a continuous nominal 1200 mm public passage from the existing entrance approach into the central reading area, ending before the rear retrieval band, and nominal 900 mm retrieval bands at every accessible shelf face. Furniture, stored bags and occupied seating envelopes belong outside those bands and door swings. Preserve the entrance opening as drawn. All five units support themselves on the floor, with removable mechanical joints and protective feet. At least one accessory relates visibly to a retained case end and the new seating, with its separation dimensioned and the shelf faces accessible. At least one upholstered sitting-contact element is replaceable. Resolve the material allocation, connection hardware, tool access and maintenance in the opening specification, then carry those decisions through the drawings and use scenes.

Audience: library users needing short browsing, companion reading and waiting seats, together with the library team and furniture workshop deciding the arrangement and furniture development.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the programme, archival dimensions, retained elements, use scenarios and source credits. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable, its proportion, format and stage. 03-archive-plan.png is the constraint reference for room and bookcase geometry, reproducing complete measured sheet 2 of HABS TENN-200. 04-archive-section.png is the constraint reference for vertical relationships, reproducing complete measured sheet 4 of HABS TENN-200. 05-archive-interior.png is the identity reference for the visible bookcases and their relationships, from interior photograph HABS TN-200-8. 06-planning-targets.png is a constraint diagram of the passage, retrieval and furniture targets. 07-companion-reading.png is an atmosphere reference for shared reading and book handling. 08-library-waiting.png is an atmosphere reference for brief seated waiting alongside active library use.

Deliverables:
1. A specification and state schedule, one document stating the five unit IDs, four sitting places, dimensional targets, material allocation, hardware types and quantities, servicing tools, largest disassembled component dimensions and the three use states
2. One dimensioned room arrangement showing the retained cases, S1, S2, C1, A1 and A2, occupied seating envelopes, the entrance approach, public passage, retrieval bands and door swings
3. One furniture overview showing all five units in relation to the retained bookcases, with the project name and programme phrase
4. Two seat drawing boards: one for S1 and S2 together, and one for C1, each with plan, front and side views, clear sitting dimensions, footprints and material callouts
5. One accessory drawing board covering A1 and A2, with the sample book and both sample bags, surface heights, footprints and the accessory-to-case separation
6. One connection and assembly board showing the five units' floor support, removable joints, hardware quantities, tool access, protective feet and the separated relationship to the retained case
7. One materials and maintenance document covering structure, sitting contact, book and bag contact, feet and joints, with named materials, surface finishes, routine cleaning and staff or technician responsibilities
8. Three separate occupied scene images: lower or middle shelf retrieval with a passing person, solo reading at S1, and companion reading at C1
9. One replacement sequence board showing removal and refitting of the upholstered sitting-contact element, its fasteners or closure and access to the supporting structure
10. One 10-second video moving through the same furniture arrangement and the three specified use states
11. One presentation document of at least eight pages, reusing the specification, arrangement, furniture drawings, connections, materials, replacement sequence and occupied scenes, with the archive credits

Acceptance:
- The specification, room arrangement, furniture overview, occupied scenes and video use the same five units S1, S2, C1, A1 and A2 and four sitting places. The overview and presentation cover print BETWEEN SHELVES and Four places, five units exactly.
- The room arrangement and presentation retain the drawn inner boundary, openings, door swings, built-ins, every bookcase footprint and every shelf tier, with both projecting-case faces and wall-case storage length and depth preserved. Dimension the 1200 mm passage and 900 mm retrieval bands, identify any traced dimensions as approximate archive-derived, and record the 22 feet 4 inches overall dimension alongside the 22 feet 3 inches dimension-chain total and their one-inch difference.
- The seat and accessory boards repeat the specification's 480 mm clear seat width, 440 mm clear depth, 450 mm seat height and 650 mm book-support height. The accessory board shows the 320 mm by 240 mm open book, two upright 300 mm by 180 mm by 400 mm bags simultaneously, and a dimensioned separation between at least one accessory and an identifiable retained case end. The presentation repeats these targets and the five-unit count.
- The connection board, replacement board and maintenance document follow the specification's material allocation and removable hardware schedule. Identify species or board type and finish for timber components, metal and finish for metal components, and fibre composition and weight in g/m2 for upholstery. Show independent floor support, protective feet, component replacement access and the largest disassembled component dimensions; assign accessible surface wiping and removable-cover handling to staff and structural joint servicing to a technician.
- The retrieval scene shows one person taking a neutral sample book from a lower or middle shelf and a second person passing on a separate route. The solo scene shows one reader at S1, S2 and C1 empty, and one bag in A2. The companion scene shows two readers at C1 using the open book on A1, two bags in A2, and S1 and S2 empty. All three scenes and the 10-second video retain the arrangement's passage, retrieval bands and furniture positions.
- The presentation contains at least eight pages and carries the credits: Historic American Buildings Survey, National Park Service, Library of Congress; Thomas Hughes Public Library, HABS TENN-200, sheets 2 and 4, Judson Mc Intire, East Tennessee Project 1973; interior photograph HABS TN-200-8, date unconfirmed in supplied metadata.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
